### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**27** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c8583f80ac47177421c9c1fb71e5e33e431ad9cf`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c8583f80ac47177421c9c1fb71e5e33e431ad9cf` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ad522bc4c40197647b519187de311f4937edbc12` — the merge of head `28a10e6f8b29849c8cf41595bc7ed213f9081972` into base `c8583f80ac47177421c9c1fb71e5e33e431ad9cf`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ad522bc4c40197647b519187de311f4937edbc12 && git checkout ad522bc4c40197647b519187de311f4937edbc12
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c8583f80ac47177421c9c1fb71e5e33e431ad9cf 28a10e6f8b29849c8cf41595bc7ed213f9081972 && git checkout -B drift-repro c8583f80ac47177421c9c1fb71e5e33e431ad9cf && git merge --no-ff 28a10e6f8b29849c8cf41595bc7ed213f9081972

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c8583f80ac47177421c9c1fb71e5e33e431ad9cf
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c8583f80ac47177421c9c1fb71e5e33e431ad9cf` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.empty-projection-unknown-count.test.ts, packages/rest/src/data-empty-projection-count-door.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/data-empty-projection-count.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts (`QueryTransportParamsSchema`, `TransportCountValueSchema`, `QueryWithTransportSchema`, `foldQueryAliasSlots`), packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts (`FindDataRequestSchema`, `HttpFindQueryParamsSchema`, `GetDataRequestSchema`), packages/spec/src/shared/lazy-schema.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-query-validation.ts (`assertProjectionFieldsExist`), packages/rest/src/crud-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/data.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, scripts/check-engine-double-contract.mjs, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, .github/workflows/ci.yml; the changeset `.changeset/26644-empty-projection-count-flag.md` read for ② only.

Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record does not pre-empt them.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. **`findData` projection (`fields`, folded from `select` / `$select`), all transports.** Before: a string was `split(',').map(trim).filter(Boolean)` and an array passed untouched, so `''`, `' '`, `','`, `' , ,'` and `[]` all became `[]`, which `assertProjectionFieldsExist` returns on (`protocol-query-validation.ts`: `if (!Array.isArray(fields) || fields.length === 0) return;`) and every driver serves as no projection. After: `projectionFieldsValue` refuses a result naming no field, `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, `param` = the spelling written (`slotParam('fields')`, the #4226 composition of `wireSpelling` and `arrivedAs`), before `engine.find` / `engine.count`. A non-empty list is split and trimmed exactly as before and still goes through `assertProjectionFieldsExist`. Absent, `undefined` and `null` keep their default (every column). Accept set after is a strict subset of before. **Right**, and it is the card's own prescription (the `pageWindowValue` precedent on the column axis).

2. **`findData` count flag (`count`, folded from `$count`), all transports.** Before: only the strings `'true'` / `'false'` were lowered; any other value stayed as it was and `countOptOut = options.count === false` read it as "count". After: `countFlagValue` parses with `QueryTransportParamsSchema.shape.count`, which is `TransportCountValueSchema.nullable().optional()` = `z.union([z.boolean(), z.enum(['true','false'])])` (data-engine.zod.ts:908, :1047), and is asked only when `options.count != null`, so `null` / absent never reach it and keep their default (count runs). Accepted: `true`, `false`, `'true'`, `'false'`. Refused: `'maybe'`, `''`, `'1'`, `'TRUE'`, `0`, `1`, anything else — `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, `param` = `$count` or `count` as written. The spec is read, not restated: `lazySchema` is a Proxy that resolves on first property access (`.shape` named in its own doc, lazy-schema.ts:20-30), so `.shape.count.safeParse` is the real schema. No `packages/spec` file is edited. **Right.** `distinct` keeps its old lowering only (`'true'` / `'false'`), untouched — it is a retired key at the HTTP declaration and not this card's parameter; noted, not a finding.

3. **`getData` projection (`GET /data/:object/:id`, `select`).** Before: `if (request.select)` — a blank string was falsy and skipped (every column), a comma-only one became `[]` (every column). After: `if (request.select != null)` and the same helper on a string or an array, `param` fixed at `select` (the only spelling that route accepts: REST `DATA_RECORD_READ_PARAMS`, dispatcher's allowlist at data.ts:268-270). Wire-reachable change: `''`, whitespace, `','` are refused. **Right** — the route's own comment (#4226, "gated exactly as on the list path") would otherwise have become false, and the card's mechanism paragraph names the shared normalizer. One non-wire edge, not a finding: an in-process caller (`action-execution.ts:546`, `select: params.select`) passing a falsy non-string such as `false` or `0` used to be skipped and now rides to `queryOptions.fields`, where `assertProjectionFieldsExist` returns on a non-array and drivers read a falsy `fields` as no projection — the same answer (every column) either way; a querystring cannot deliver it.

4. **Every door that takes `$count` / `count` or a projection (seat question 2).** Read every `.findData(` / `.getData(` caller outside tests at the head:
   - `RestServer GET /data/:object` (crud-routes.ts:158-164): the whole `req.query` to `findData` → both refusals, `mapDataError` keeps the 400. Agrees.
   - `RestServer POST /data/:object/query` (crud-routes.ts:347-367): `FindDataRequestSchema.safeParse` first. `QueryWithTransportSchema` extends `QueryTransportParamsSchema.shape` (data-engine.zod.ts:1379-1382), so `count: 'maybe'` is refused there as `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` (pre-existing, unchanged); `select: ''` (`z.string()`), `$select: ','` and `fields: []` (`z.array`) pass the schema and are refused by `findData`. Agrees. Two codes for the count family at this one door (`VALIDATION_FAILED` at the schema, `VALIDATION_ERROR` at the normalizer) is the pre-existing split the `$top` window already has; not widened here.
   - runtime dispatcher `GET /data/:object` (data.ts:409-433): querystring rides verbatim to `callData('query')` → `protocol.findData` (action-execution.ts:703-709). Agrees.
   - runtime dispatcher `POST /data/:object/query` (data.ts:200-260): the same `FindDataRequestSchema` gate, then `callData('query')` → `findData`. Agrees (same shape as REST; the count arm is schema-refused on both).
   - runtime dispatcher `GET /data/:object/:id` (data.ts:263-274): `select` allowlisted, `callData('get')` → `getData`. Agrees, 400.
   - `RestServer GET /data/:object/:id` (crud-routes.ts:179-229): `getData`, but the catch rewrites every 400 to 404 — see item 5.
   - `GET /data/:object/export` (data-action-routes.ts:1256-1285) builds a canonical AST with no `fields` and no `count`; the job reads (data-action-routes.ts:440-447, :845-853), `import-runner.ts` (`findArgsBase` spreads the caller's request; its three call sites name no projection), `connector-pull.ts:343` and the in-process action path pass no projection or a named one. None reaches either refusal. The PR body's door table is complete and correct; the export door it omits is unaffected.
   - No other reader of `$count` exists in any `packages/*/src` outside spec and tests (the only hit is a driver-memory aggregation-stage comment). `ODataQuerySchema.$count` (`z.boolean()`) is consumed only by `OData.buildUrl`, not a door. **No runtime door is still lenient.** The one surface still wider than the door is a published DECLARATION, not a door: `HttpFindQueryParamsSchema` (protocol.zod.ts:2367-2385) declares `count: z.coerce.boolean()` (admits `'maybe'`, and reads `'false'` as `true`) and `select: z.string()` (admits a blank); it has no runtime reader at the head (grep: only CHANGELOG prose and two comments cite it). That drift pre-exists this PR and is in `packages/spec` — escalated in ③, not a defect of this diff.

5. **REST by-id answers the empty projection at 404 (seat question 3).** `res.status(mapped.status === 400 ? 404 : mapped.status)` is at crud-routes.ts:229 on `origin/main` byte-for-byte; the diff does not touch crud-routes.ts. On main, `?select=nope` on that route already answers `404 INVALID_FIELD` through the same line (the door test measures it at the head). So the PR creates no new 404-for-bad-input PATH; it adds one more input class to a pre-existing rewrite's reach, and the dev pinned the status as "whatever this route gives an unknown select field" rather than a literal 404 — the honest pin. **Pre-existing, outside this card's surface, judged right to leave alone.** What it leaves is a transport split (REST 404 vs dispatcher 400 for one input), which pre-exists for `INVALID_FIELD` and now covers `VALIDATION_ERROR` too — that needs its own carrier (③).

6. **Public surface.** `projectionFieldsValue`, `countFlagValue` and `quotedQueryValue` are module-private functions in protocol.ts; no export, type or signature of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` changes; `QueryTransportParamsSchema` was already exported from `@objectstack/spec/data` and imported in the same block that already carries `QueryPageWindowParamSchema`. No `packages/spec/**` path in the diff. **No public-surface change — right.**

7. **Clause-② (seat question 1).** `clause2-line.mjs` reserves `yes (narrowing)` for "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another" and defines `no (narrowing)` as "NOT a widening, but breaking. This is the whole point of the arm." Measured on the diff: no new accepted spelling (the `$`-alias table and slot table are untouched), no new accepted value (both accept sets shrink, item 1-2), no new door (every caller list unchanged), no export change (item 6). The triage's "declare `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`" named the wrong arm for this diff; the dev's `no (narrowing)` on both the PR body and the changeset is the correct reading, and the seat's acceptance of it is **confirmed**. The dev's reason that "pm-dispatch execution-duties says a card narrowing a published accept set is Clause-② no" could not be located verbatim in `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**` at the head; the ruling stands on the one reader (`clause2-line.mjs`) alone, which is enough.

8. **Error code.** The refusals carry `VALIDATION_ERROR`; the `$top=` precedent they mirror carries `INVALID_REQUEST`. The card's done-when binds status 400 and the named parameter ("as `$top=` is"), not the code; the triage ruling names no code. Two adjacent refusals of one normalizer now carry two codes. Not a contract defect (both are 400, both set `param`), **right as ordered**, recorded so a later unification is read as the error-contract change it would be.

9. **`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` (seat question 4).** The diff is one ADDED entry (`protocol.empty-projection-unknown-count.test.ts`, verb `findOne`, pinned 2); no existing entry's file, verb or count changes. `check-engine-double-contract.mjs` `retainedErrors` (lines 2797-2815) makes the GROWTH direction an error — "pins N engine double(s) that the pinned ledger does not record … Run --write and commit" — so the new test's double (its `findOne` routed through `assertEngineFindOnePredicate`, as the test shows) requires exactly this entry. The loss direction reds only when a file's live pin count falls below its ledger entry; no existing entry moved. **A pin addition the new test requires; nothing loosened.** The count `2` is the gate's own census and is not re-derivable read-only; `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` on the head (in progress) is its verdict.

10. **Tests as contract pins.** The protocol file pins code, status, `param`, the quoted value (bounded at 64 chars) and that the engine spies were never called, for every refused spelling, plus the preservation set (projection lists, `count` absent / true / false / null, by-id select string / array / undefined / null). The REST and dispatcher files pin each door over a real SQLite driver with a per-object read counter at zero across the refusals, the controls answering as before, and (dispatcher) both host exits agreeing. Red-first on the base is declared per file with counts; not re-run here (read-only), and the dev's counts are the only evidence of it. Adequate for the accept-set claims above.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch`, header `fix(metadata-protocol)!: …`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` as the first thing after the colon on both the PR body and the changeset body, `Metadata-protocol: none` beside it on both, the `**BREAKING**` banner, and one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker with its reason. `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` are green on the head.

Nothing a metadata author writes changes here (no schema key, no authorable surface, no export), so `none` is true and `patch` is the only level the gate accepts beside it. The older docblock sentence "during the launch window a breaking change ships minor" (line 1794) is the pre-ruling-A coupling the same file says it lost; the check-run on the head is green with `patch`.
- The changeset's Before / Now / Unchanged / Who-sees-it / Remedy paragraphs match the diff clause for clause, including that `POST …/query` already refused a non-boolean `count` at the body schema and still does.
- Moved package: only `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` has a source change; the two other packages carry new tests only. Correct.
- **Clause-②:** `no (narrowing)` — judged in ① item 7; matches the diff, matches the changeset, matches the `(narrowing)` arm the ADR-0087 gate and the queue guard read.

Verified at the head (protocol.zod.ts:2367-2385).
